body.hook: Your band instrument might be the most expensive thing you've ever been responsible for. Brass and woodwind instruments are precise machines: a bent rod, a dented slide or a dropped mouthpiece can stop an instrument from playing. Learning to assemble, hold and care for it properly is the first skill every musician learns.

study.title: Instrument Care Station
study.question: How do I set up and care for my instrument?
study.passage:
Part 1, Assembly demonstration (10 minutes): Sit in sections. The teacher demonstrates assembly for each instrument family:
• Flute: twist the headjoint and footjoint gently; never push on the keys or rods.
• Clarinet and saxophone: grease corks lightly; moisten the reed; line up the reed with the mouthpiece tip and tighten the ligature gently. Hold the clarinet's middle joints without squeezing the rings and keys.
• Trumpet, trombone, French horn, euphonium and tuba: insert the mouthpiece with a gentle twist, never by banging it. Check the slides and valves move freely.
• Percussion: check sticks and mallets, and stand at the correct height for the snare and bells.
Part 2, Posture check (5 minutes): Sit tall at the front of the chair, feet flat, shoulders relaxed, instrument brought to you (not you to it).
Part 3, Breathing (5 minutes): Breathe in for 4 counts through the mouth, filling low in the body, then breathe out for 8 counts on a "ssss" sound.
Part 4, First sound (10 minutes): Mouthpiece only for brass (buzz), mouthpiece and barrel or neck for woodwinds, headjoint only for flute. Make a steady sound for 4 counts.
Part 5, Care and storage (5 minutes): Swab or dry the instrument, remove and store reeds in a reed case, close the case latches, and store the case flat.

examples.title: Assembly
examples.problem: How do you put a mouthpiece into a trumpet?
examples.answer: Insert it with a gentle twist so it doesn't get stuck

examples.title: Reeds
examples.problem: How should a clarinet reed be stored?
examples.answer: Remove it, dry it and store it in a reed case

examples.title: Posture
examples.answer: Sit at the front of the chair, back tall, feet flat and shoulders relaxed

examples.title: Breathing
examples.problem: Why breathe in low and deep?
examples.answer: Low, full breaths give more air and better control
